chief_complaint: annual physical for high school soccer clearance
hpi_details: A 16-year-old male presents to the clinic for an annual physical and high school soccer clearance. The patient reports no current symptoms.
ideas: He thinks he is in great physical shape and only needs a quick check to make sure he is ready for the upcoming soccer season.
concerns: He is worried that an unexpected health issue might keep him from getting cleared to play on the soccer team this season.
expectations: He hopes to walk out with his signed athletic clearance form today so he can hand it in before tryouts start tomorrow.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Adolescent Sports Physical evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Adolescent Sports Physical is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes cardiac auscultation with Valsalva maneuver to screen for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and reviewing Tdap/HPV vaccination status, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: annual physical for high school soccer clearance
Key HPI features: A 16-year-old male presents to the clinic for an annual physical and high school soccer clearance. The patient reports no current symptoms.
Objective/Exam findings: Normal vital signs and BMI, normal cardiac auscultation including with Valsalva maneuver, no murmurs, normal musculoskeletal screening exam.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Adolescent Sports Physical.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Exertional syncope or chest pain.
management_principles: Plan for Adolescent Sports physical: Valsalva cardiac auscultation for HCM, check Tdap/HPV vaccines
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

teaching.one_liner: A pre-participation exam focused on cardiac screening questions to rule out risk of sudden cardiac death, plus vaccine catch-up.
differentials: Occult cardiac disease with exertional symptoms
red_flags: Family history of sudden death before 50

must_ask.say: Any chest pain or fainting during exercise?
Any sudden deaths in the family at a young age?
Which vaccines are up to date?
How much screen time and sleep do you get?
Anything you'd like to discuss privately?

history.answer: I'm here for my annual physical and sports clearance so I can play on the high school soccer team.
I really hope we can get my sports clearance form signed today so I can turn it in to my coach before tryouts tomorrow.
I feel completely fine and don't have any pain, tiredness, or health complaints.
I had a routine health screening about three years ago in middle school, and everything was completely normal.
I received all my childhood immunizations, had a tetanus booster a few years back, and got a flu shot last winter, but I'm not sure if I completed the HPV series.
My grandfather has type 2 diabetes diagnosed in his seventies, but no one in my family has had cancer or heart attacks at a young age.
I eat three regular meals a day, drink plenty of water, and practice soccer three to four afternoons a week.
My weight has stayed steady while I grew taller over the past year, and I've never tried or needed to diet.
I handle cold and heat normally, and my bowel movements are regular every day without constipation.
I sleep soundly about eight hours a night without snoring, and my knees and joints feel great even after running hard.
I have never had chest tightness, pain, pressure, or a fluttering heartbeat while exercising or playing sports.
I have never passed out, fainted, or felt dizzy or lightheaded during or right after intense exercise.
I get tired after long sprints just like my teammates, but I catch my breath quickly and never have severe shortness of breath.
No one in my family has ever died suddenly, had an unexplained drowning, or had serious heart disease before age fifty.

exam.finding: Well-developed, athletic adolescent male in no acute distress.
Blood pressure 116/72 mmHg, heart rate 68 bpm, respiratory rate 14 breaths/min, body temperature 36.6 C, SpO2 99%, BMI 21.2 kg/m2.
Regular rate and rhythm with normal S1 and S2; no murmurs, gallops, or clicks in supine position or during Valsalva maneuver.
Clear breath sounds bilaterally without wheezing, rales, or rhonchi.
Bilateral radial and femoral pulses are strong, symmetric, and without radiofemoral delay.
Thyroid gland is normal in size, non-tender, and symmetric without nodules or thyromegaly.
Normal skin turgor without jaundice, purple abdominal striae, or abnormal rashes.
Full active and passive range of motion in bilateral shoulders, elbows, wrists, hips, knees, and ankles without swelling or tenderness.
Normal spinal alignment on Adams forward bend test with no scoliosis, midline vertebral tenderness, or limitation of motion.
